inputs.text:
More than 58 lakh names have been removed from the electoral roll, and the Supreme Court has ordered tribunals to hear challenges—yet those tribunals are not even operational. That is no way to administer an election. A trustworthy vote depends on accurate rolls and lawful, timely hearings, not bureaucratic drift.

Authorities must get the tribunals working and apply the rules consistently. When basic procedures fail, confidence suffers and political opportunists gain room to stir suspicion. Protecting the integrity of the roll and giving people a fair hearing are both duties of the state.
